solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This person's two ducks causing damage

parts.note: the setter speaking: this person is I, so this person's is I'M, I am
in cricket a pair is two ducks, out for nought in both innings

explanation.surface: A batsman's double failure brings harm to the team.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pair' is cricket slang for scoring zero (a duck) in both innings of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it, a straight synonym of damage as a verb.

clue.text: Why things go wrong with potato salad?

parts.note: murphy is an old slang word for a potato, from the Irish surname
slaw, as in coleslaw, is a shredded cabbage salad

explanation.surface: A picnic disaster blamed on the potato salad.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break moves: MURPHY + SLAW is read as MURPHY'S LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy's Law is the joking principle that anything that can go wrong will, so it explains mishaps.

clue.text: Bath's water has Virginia lifting leg

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the abbreviation is read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Someone in a bath raises a leg out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is the English city, not a tub; the River Avon flows through it.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Avon runs through the city of Bath, so it is that city's river.

clue.text: Materialize, retaining form, and change category

indicators.note: retaining means the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: to reify is to make something abstract concrete, to materialize it
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: An instruction to make something real, keep its shape, then file it under a new heading.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclassify is to assign something to a different class or grouping.

clue.text: Unwell after stench from pit comes to town

indicators.note: after means the word for unwell follows the stench in the answer

parts.note: BO, body odour, is the smell from an armpit
feeling rough means feeling unwell

explanation.surface: A miner feels sick after the smell from the colliery reaches the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pit' suggests a mine but means the armpit.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is a town with its own local council, a municipal district.

clue.text: Beginning to climb in French south, sweep across sky

indicators.note: in says the opening letter is placed inside the French word

parts.note: sud is French for south

indicators.note: beginning to says to take only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Starting an ascent in the south of France as clouds race overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds scud when they are driven fast across the sky by the wind.

clue.text: Led in by Duff, everyone entering cul-de-sac

indicators.note: entering says the word for everyone goes inside the jumbled letters
duff means faulty or useless, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone is guided by a man called Duff while a crowd pours into a dead end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duff' looks like a person's name but is the anagram indicator turning LED IN BY into BLINDEY, which ALL enters.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind alley is a street closed at one end, the same as a dead-end road.

clue.text: Rather small-minded Republican brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the abbreviation is put inside the word for small-minded

parts.note: petty means small-minded, mean in outlook

explanation.surface: A political verdict that a narrow-minded Republican was recruited.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty used as an adverb, as in pretty good, means fairly or rather.

clue.text: Mark turning to Nick for school folder?

indicators.note: turning says the word for mark is written backwards

parts.note: to note is to mark or observe
to nick or collar someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A teacher converts a mark into a scratch on a ring binder.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's famous fee-paying school; its traditional broad stiff collar is folded over the jacket, hence 'school folder?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A collar is folded around the neck, and the Eton collar belongs to that school's uniform.

clue.text: Bundle of nerves totalled old car on short trip

indicators.note: on says the jumbled letters come after the trip in this across answer

parts.note: a spin is a short drive or outing

indicators.note: a car that is totalled is wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous wreck after writing off a vintage car during a brief jaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinal cord is the thick column of nerve tissue running down the backbone.

clue.text: Nothing uses present tense

parts.note: now means at present
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A grammar note that nothing is written in the present tense.
explanation.walkthrough: NOWT is northern English dialect for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowt is a dialect word meaning not a thing, the opposite of owt (anything).

clue.text: Revolutionary band on road in ancient port

definitions.meaning: the rubber band on a wheel that revolves on the road
An ancient Phoenician port, now in Lebanon

explanation.definitionFit: A wheel's tyre turns as it rolls, and Tyre was a Phoenician harbour city.

clue.text: Director of great intellect capturing scene after evacuation

indicators.note: capturing means the genius's name holds the remaining letters inside it

parts.note: Albert Einstein is the byword for a great intellect

indicators.note: a word evacuated has its insides emptied out, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A brilliant film-maker takes in a shot once the set has been cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein was the Soviet film director of Battleship Potemkin.

clue.text: Older man spooning sweetly?

parts.note: spooning means canoodling, and also ladling sugar; an older man courting a younger partner with gifts

explanation.surface: An elderly gent stirring sugar into his tea, or courting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spooning' is old slang for kissing and cuddling, but also suggests a spoon of sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar daddy is a rich older man who lavishes money on a younger lover.

clue.text: Pulling back or turning in

definitions.meaning: ... is withdrawal, as an army's ... from the field
going to bed, turning in for the night

explanation.definitionFit: To retire is both to withdraw from a position and to go to bed at night.

clue.text: Faint suggestion for audience becoming less loud

indicators.note: for an audience means the phrase is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: dim means faint and an innuendo is a suggestion, a sly hint

explanation.surface: A quiet hint to the listeners as the music fades.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminuendo is the musical term for a gradual decrease in volume.

clue.text: Credit cards to hold out in photo

indicators.note: in says the verb phrase goes inside the word for photo

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
to last is to hold out, endure

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their bank cards out of sight in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' looks like the instruction but 'to hold out' is the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is slang for credit or debit cards, made of plastic, as in paying with plastic.

clue.text: Coming from spaceship to LEM you see stargazer

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An astronaut aboard a lunar module is told to look out for an astronomer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'see stargazer' does not substitute for the answer: 'see' is a link word joining wordplay to definition, and 'stargazer' alone defines it. LEM is the Apollo lunar module.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy was the Alexandrian astronomer whose earth-centred model of the heavens held for centuries.

clue.text: Circle lake bed first

indicators.note: first says the word for bed comes before the lake in the answer

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A lakeside campsite where the beds are set out first.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people, a circle of friends.

clue.text: Two dozen for we nutty cooks

indicators.note: cooks as a verb means fiddles or doctors, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A batch of two dozen made by an eccentric baker for the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' looks like a noun but is a verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two dozen is two twelves, which makes twenty-four.

clue.text: Channel swimmer crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the fish's name lies across, around, the abbreviation

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: Someone swimming the English Channel passes a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel swimmer' suggests a cross-Channel athlete; the swimmer is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch, a channel dug in the ground.

clue.text: Pull from Asian beast carrying unspecified number

indicators.note: carrying means the animal holds the letter inside it

parts.note: the yak is a Himalayan ox
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Tugging something off a Tibetan pack animal loaded with goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to give a sudden hard tug, a forceful pull.

clue.text: Go without nookie?

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, without, as in ex dividend
it is a coy word for sex, as nookie is

explanation.surface: A cheeky question whether to leave if there is no sex on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to leave or depart, the verb sense of go.

clue.text: Where traders are quick to catch morning boat

indicators.note: to catch means the word for quick holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: fleet means fast, quick
AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
the ark is Noah's boat

explanation.surface: Merchants hurry to make the early ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is a street market selling secondhand goods, where many stallholders trade.

clue.text: Lot having eaten all the pies finally replete?

parts.note: who ate all the pies? is a football chant mocking someone fat

indicators.note: finally says to take only the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A glutton who has stuffed himself is wondering about his fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who ate all the pies?' is a British football terrace chant at an overweight player.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's fortune in life, one's fate.

clue.text: Low resistance up in space

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Weak electrical resistance high up in outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective but is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means space, as in room to move or no room left.

clue.text: Greek lost in Antioch beginning to revive within

indicators.note: within says the opening letter goes inside the scrambled letters
lost suggests being at sea, so the letters of the words before it are scrambled
beginning to says to take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A Greek traveller missing in the ancient city of Antioch starts to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' scrambles IN ANTIOCH into CO_INTHIAN, and R from 'revive' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Corinthian is a native of the Greek city of Corinth, so a Greek.

clue.text: Feisty female Doctor Who at last seen in play

indicators.note: seen in means the pieces appear inside the word for play

parts.note: to toy is to play
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

indicators.note: at last says to take only the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A spirited heroine finally turns up in a Doctor Who drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' reads as the TV series but splits into Doctor (MB) and the last letter of Who.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomboy is a girl who likes rough, boisterous activities, a feisty girl.
